newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber prices extend fall at close.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber prices extend fall at close.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices extended their falls at the close on lack of fresh overseas demand, dealers said.
They said a weaker Tokyo market also weighed on prices.
"It has been very quiet this week. We are still waiting for fresh inquiries from consumers," said one dealer.
He said he heard some business was done but it was mostly short-covering among brokers. "The amount involved was very small," the dealer added.
Dealers noted many sellers in the market as supply of raw materials was returning to normal due to improving weather.

At the close, February RSS1 buyer and SMR 20 buyer were quoted at 310.50 cents ($1.25) and 306.50 cents ($1.23) a kg respectively by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, both down a cent from Tuesday.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 307 cents a kg, SMR CV at 369, SMR L at 350, SMR 5 at 319, SMR 10 at 308 and drum latex FOB at 241.
The INRO five-day moving average was 241.32 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Jan 7 against 241.81 on Jan 6. The daily indicator price was 239.34 versus 241.04.
